academy.label: Academy / Firefighter I-II
academy.summary: Fire behavior, construction, SCBA, hose, ladders, search, ventilation and Mayday fundamentals.
guide: Fire behavior
Heat transfer, ventilation-limited fire, flow paths, door control and cooling.
Construction
Common systems, lightweight components, concealed spaces and collapse indicators.
PPE/SCBA
Inspection, donning, emergency procedures, crew integrity and air management.
Hose/ladders/search
Line movement, nozzle control, ladder use, coordinated search and victim removal.
Ventilation/Mayday
Coordinate openings with suppression; practice emergency traffic and self-rescue.
cards: Flow path?
Route heated gases, smoke and air move between higher- and lower-pressure areas/openings.
Why can opening a door worsen conditions?
It may add oxygen and strengthen a flow path before suppression is ready.
Low-air alarm means?
Act on department air-management policy; it is not a target for remaining inside.
Why learn construction?
It affects hidden fire spread, access, collapse potential and tactical options.
Why coordinate ventilation?
Openings can change fire behavior and interior conditions.
quiz: Before forcing a smoke-charged exterior door?
Coordinate opening with line/search plan and read conditions
Recognize operational fire-spread and structural risks
next: Log hands-on repetitions, not just test scores.
Ask instructors what good performance looks like.
Run a decision sim after each major topic.

probation.label: Probation / First 100 Shifts
probation.summary: Turn academy knowledge into dependable company performance and crew trust.
guide: Apparatus
Tool locations, hose loads, daily checks and common failure points.
District
Routes, target hazards, hydrants/static water, access and recurring occupancies.
Company expectations
Checks, chores, training, radio habits, documentation and station etiquette.
Core skills
Repeat stretches, ladders, forcing, masking, search, water supply and reset.
Feedback
Ask what to notice/do sooner next time, then repeat the behavior.
cards: Useful end-of-shift goal?
One thing learned, one skill repeated and one question answered.
Why memorize tool locations?
It reduces searching and frees attention for the assignment.
Strong feedback question?
What would you want me to notice or do sooner next time?
What belongs in a career log?
De-identified training, skills, experience, feedback and achievements.
More valuable than random certs?
Fundamentals, documented experience, crew trust and role-aligned training.
quiz: You cannot find a tool during a drill.
Review the related equipment system and practice deployment
Use the miss to strengthen apparatus familiarity.
Corrective feedback is most useful when you:
Translate it into a behavior and repeat the skill
Observable change is the point of feedback.
next: Clear one apparatus weak spot each shift.
